title: The Great Generational Wealth Divide — TikTok
notes: Story arc: hook question → the boom → they took over D.C. → the rules they wrote → housing → the bill for younger generations → the $84T handoff (and who gets it) → the fix.
All figures are from the article (Mar 18, 2026). Where the article names a source it's shown on screen; otherwise the article itself is credited.
Photos: Wikimedia Commons. Clips: Pixabay. Credits print on screen and are listed in credits.md.

post.caption: Boomers own about half of America's wealth. Millennials hold almost half its debt. How did one generation end up with so much, and what happens to the $84 trillion they're about to pass down?

headline.text: Boomers own half of America's wealth.

say: Baby Boomers own about half of all the wealth in America.
Millennials? They hold almost half of all the debt.
So how did one generation end up with so much?
We dug into it, and the answer starts with timing.

scenes.query: Children of the United States in the 1950s
say: Between 1946 and 1964, seventy-six million babies were born,
and the country reorganized itself around them.
California was building a new school every week.
Then, in 1976, the first Boomers could run for Congress.
They took over, and Congress aged right along with them.

scenes.source: Generation Distribution of Congress · American Inequality
say: At their peak, Boomers held sixty percent of Congress,
while making up only a quarter of the country.

scenes.title: The rules they wrote
scenes.source: The Great Generational Wealth Divide · American Inequality
say: And they wrote the rules for people like them:
limits on new housing, taxes that favor wealth, protected retirements.

overlays.label: of all U.S. real estate wealth is owned by Boomers

say: Which brings us to housing.
Boomers own forty-one percent of all real estate wealth, often big empty-nest homes.

scenes.title: New homes with 4+ bedrooms
scenes.source: The Great Generational Wealth Divide · American Inequality
say: Builders followed the money. In the seventies, one in five new homes had four-plus bedrooms.
Now it's nearly half.

overlays.label: of all U.S. debt is held by Millennials

say: Meanwhile, younger Americans got the bill.
Millennials hold forty-one percent of all debt, almost double the Boomers.
Now the biggest handoff in history is underway: eighty-four trillion dollars.

scenes.title: Every $100 of Boomer wealth
scenes.source: The Great Generational Wealth Divide · American Inequality (2022)
say: But it won't be spread evenly.
The top ten percent of Boomers hold seventy-one percent of it.
Boomers grew up in abundance. The question is whether it gets shared:
more homes, cheaper college, higher wages.
The full story is on American Inequality. Link in bio.
